Population stability index and Jensen-Shannon divergence (C backend)

Source: R/drift.R
drftpsi.Rd

Two effect sizes of how far the distribution of a numeric column has moved from a reference sample. Both samples are binned on the reference's quantiles and the two sets of bin shares compared. Unlike a p-value they do not grow with the sample size, so they say how large a shift is rather than whether it is detectable.

Usage

drftpsi(x, y, bins = 10L, eps = 1e-06)

Arguments

x, y

Numeric vectors, the reference and the new sample; logical vectors are read as 0/1.

bins

The number of quantile bins of the reference, one whole number from 2 to 1,000,000; fewer are used when quantiles tie.

eps

The floor of an empty bin in the index, in (0, 1). It is part of the statistic: compare runs at one eps.

Value

A named numeric vector of class drftpsi: psi and jsdiv, with the inputs in the attribute lakner.

Details

Binning: values are rounded to 12 significant digits (so a formatting difference between two releases does not move tied values across an edge), the bins + 1 type-7 quantiles of x are computed, duplicates removed, and the interior quantiles become right-closed cut points with open ends. When the reference has fewer than three distinct quantiles, every distinct quantile is a cut point instead.

The population stability index is \(\sum_i (p_i - q_i)\log(p_i/q_i)\) over the reference shares \(p_i\) and the new shares \(q_i\): the symmetrised Kullback-Leibler divergence. The conventional reading, from credit-risk monitoring where it originates, is below 0.1 stable, 0.1 to 0.25 worth a look, above 0.25 a material shift; these bands are heuristics with no calibrated null distribution, and on a few hundred rows binning noise alone can exceed 0.25. The Jensen-Shannon divergence \(\tfrac12 KL(p\|m) + \tfrac12 KL(q\|m)\), \(m = (p+q)/2\), is bounded by \(\log 2\) nats, so it compares across columns with different numbers of bins, and is finite when a bin is empty on one side. Empty bins are floored at eps for the index only.

References

Wu D, Olson DL (2010). Enterprise risk management: coping with model risk in a large bank. Journal of the Operational Research Society 61(2), 179–190. doi:10.1057/jors.2008.144

Lin J (1991). Divergence measures based on the Shannon entropy. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 37(1), 145–151. doi:10.1109/18.61115

See also

drftks().

Examples

set.seed(2)
ref <- stats::rnorm(500)
drftpsi(ref, stats::rnorm(500))
#> drftpsi: psi = 0.022072, jsdiv = 0.002753 
#> inputs: nx = 500, ny = 500, bins = 10 
drftpsi(ref, stats::rnorm(500, mean = 1))
#> drftpsi: psi = 0.9543, jsdiv = 0.1053 
#> inputs: nx = 500, ny = 500, bins = 10 
drftpsi(ref, ref)
#> drftpsi: psi = 0, jsdiv = 0 
#> inputs: nx = 500, ny = 500, bins = 10 
drftpsi(c(1, 1, 1), c(9, 9, 9))[["jsdiv"]] <= log(2)
#> [1] TRUE
drftpsi(ref, stats::rnorm(500, mean = 1), bins = 4, eps = 0.01)
#> drftpsi: psi = 0.69315, jsdiv = 0.08235 
#> inputs: nx = 500, ny = 500, bins = 4 
try(drftpsi(ref, ref, bins = 1))
#> Error : drftpsi: `bins` must be one whole number of at least 2.
